findings.description: `truncate-end` on the confirm prompt cuts the end of a long unblock reason. The reason, the `— unblock?` question and the y/n hint go with it. The code comment in `use-controls.hook.ts` says the operator must be shown the whole reason before unblocking.
findings.body:
**The confirm prompt now cuts off the unblock reason, the question, and the y/n hint**

This PR makes the confirm prompt a single truncated row:
```tsx
<Text wrap="truncate-end">
  <Text color="yellow">{prompt.question}</Text>
  <Text dimColor> (y/n, Esc cancels)</Text>
</Text>
```
The `u` key builds its question from the stored block reason (`use-controls.hook.ts:409-416`):
```ts
// The reason first, and read from the store rather than typed by the
// operator: unblocking is a claim that the block was addressed, and
// nobody can make that claim about a reason they were never shown.
question: `${blocked.id} was blocked: ${selectedBlockedReason(owner.deps, blocked.id)} — unblock?`,
```
Some block reasons are much longer than a terminal row:
- `'re-steer failed — session unreachable'` makes the line about 90 characters.
- The `SteerNotDeliveredError` messages (`session-runtime.service.ts:1024-1035`) are about 190-230 characters on their own.

At 80 columns the end of the line is cut, which removes the cause, `— unblock?` and `(y/n, Esc cancels)`. Nothing else on screen shows the reason:
- The sessions row shows only `blocked (N rejections)`.
- `DashboardSession` has no field for the reason.
- The detail pane has no section for it.

Before this PR, Ink's default wrap showed the whole line.

Possible fixes:
- Keep `— unblock? (y/n, Esc cancels)` intact and truncate only the reason. For example, put the hint in its own `flexShrink={0}` `Text` inside a row `Box`.
- Or let the confirm prompt wrap, and have `App` count its rows from `stdout.columns`.

The kill question is affected in a milder way: with its hint it is about 87 columns, so the hint is clipped at 80.

findings.description: The stale-radar notice is not truncated. In a fleet it is about 70 columns wide, so on a narrower terminal it takes two rows while `App` counts one, and the frame reaches the terminal's height again.
findings.body:
**The stale-radar notice can still wrap, which brings back the flicker**

```tsx
{radarStale ? (
  <Text dimColor>{`${lead}conflict radar off — start it with \`pup watch --start\``}</Text>
) : null}
```
`App` counts this line as one row (`app.component.tsx:97-100` adds `snapshot.radarStale ? 1 : 0` to `radarUsed`), but the line has no `wrap` setting. ADR 0121 says "every line counted as one row is truncated … so a narrow terminal cannot add rows the count did not see".

The notice shows for every project whose watcher has never run, because `radarStale` is `!beat || …` (`dashboard.service.ts:129`). In a fleet, the line is 68 characters with the 12-character project lead, plus 2 columns for the root `paddingX`. So it wraps below about 70 columns in a fleet, and below about 56 for a single project.

When the table is windowed the frame is exactly `rows - 1` tall, so one wrapped row makes it `rows`. Ink then clears and redraws every 2 s, which is the flicker this PR fixes.

Example: `pup ui --all` over two projects with no watcher and 30 planned tasks, in a 65-column tmux pane. The stale-radar test does not catch this because ink-testing-library renders at 100 columns.

89411a5 truncated the header, prompt and read-only lines but missed this one.

findings.description: The merge pane's title (`pup merge <id> --pr (done — Enter or Esc closes)`) is counted as one row in `App`'s `mergeLogLines` but has no `wrap`, so in a narrow pane (about 58 columns or fewer) it takes two rows and the frame reaches the terminal height; give it `wrap="truncate-end"`.

The table's `+N more` line is always drawn below the window, so with the cursor near the end of the list (every hidden row above) it reads as "more below"; split the count into above and below, or also mark the top.

`stdout.rows ?? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` only catches `undefined`. A TTY that reports 0 rows (e.g. `docker exec -t` before its first resize) collapses the table to one row plus `+N more`; `stdout.rows || Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` would treat 0 as unknown.

'puts the detail pane where the table was' passes even if Enter does nothing: at 24 rows `t-plan5` is never in the window and `s-live0-1` is already in the table. Assert `not.toContain('t-plan0')` and that the pane's own text (e.g. `(Esc closes)`) is present.

'keeps a long prompt to one row' never truncates anything: the kill question plus its hint (~87 chars) fits ink-testing-library's 100-column frame, so removing `wrap="truncate-end"` would still pass. The input prompt's `truncate-start` has no test at all.

The height sweep covers only one project with the conductor stopped. The baseline line, status line, merge log, `unreadable` stores and fleets of more than two projects are never rendered, so drift in those hand counts (which ADR 0121 relies on this test to catch) goes unnoticed.
`viewport.utils.ts` says the tests pin it, but `sectionShare` and `usedLines` have no direct tests, `clip` lacks `max` 0/1 and empty-list cases, and `windowStart` is never tested with `total < size`.

`DEPS` is character-identical to `dashboard-components.test.ts:34`, and `sessionAt`/`snapshot` re-implement the `sessionFixture`/`snapshotFixture` builders already in `dashboard-components.test.ts` and `controls.test.ts`; reuse their `Partial<>`-override shape.
`await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 0))` is repeated inline at lines 87, 127, 174 and 197; a local `tick()` helper (or one shared with `controls.test.ts`) would name the flush once.
The 'draws everything' assertion `not.toMatch(/\+\d+ more\s*$/m)` only catches a `+N more` at end of line; plain `not.toMatch(/\+\d+ more/)` is stricter.
`moreLine` bakes in a two-space indent that `Debt` and `Radar` both `.trim()` away; only `App` uses the indent, so return the bare `+N more` and let `App` indent its own line.

The `liveCount` prop gives `Sessions` a second source of truth only to keep "no live sessions" correct when windowed; `App` already computes `live.length === 0` for `fixedRows` and could draw that line itself.

About 25 lines of windowing arithmetic (`tableLines`, `fixedRows`, `fits`, `windowSize`, `start`/`end`, the slices) sit inline in `App` beside `viewport.utils.ts`, so they can only be tested by rendering `App`; `debtShare` and `radarShare` are also the same call twice.

New tests belong at `test/unit/<path under src>/` (docs/conventions/testing.md §Layout; ADR 0116 says new code follows it), e.g. `test/unit/cli/ui/viewport-utils.test.ts`; this file is colocated in `src/cli/ui/` like its older siblings.
"The frame is at most one row short of the terminal" reads backwards: `body = terminalRows - 1 - chrome` makes it at least one row short.
The comment says these are "Lines the frame spends before any list", but the prompt, footer and merge pane render after the lists; "outside the lists" is accurate.

process_issues.description: The conventions reviewer reported that it did not read the component diffs (app, debt, footer, header, prompt, radar, sessions, use-controls), so conventions coverage of those production files is partial. Its review covered the test layout, the ADR format and file naming.
